clue.text: Fail this manoeuvring, causing skid

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving things about, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver botches a manoeuvre and the car slides out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: When a vehicle's rear end swings from side to side on a slippery road, it is said to slide like a swimming fish's tail.

clue.text: Join parade and collapse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: soldiers take their places in ranks
second meaning: a roof or structure caves inward

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a soldier fainting on parade; the two halves are separate senses of one phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb is both the military order to line up and a description of a ceiling caving down.

clue.text: Insect trapper upset married students

indicators.note: upset means turned over, which in a down clue flips the letters end to end

parts.note: wed means married
the NUS is the UK's National Union of Students

explanation.surface: A newly married student couple are upset by a bug catcher.
explanation.definitionFit: The sundew is a carnivorous bog plant that catches insects on sticky hairs.

clue.text: In plants uranium has leaked across — it's all over!

indicators.note: all over suggests turning everything over, so the letters run backwards
has means holds, so one word contains the other

parts.note: spilt means leaked or overflowed, here spread across
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Radioactive material escapes at a power plant, and it is game over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plants' looks like power plants in the surface; it is the definition. SPILT holds U, then the whole is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulips are spring-flowering bulbs, an example of garden flowers.

clue.text: Conclude New York is full? Like hell

parts.note: to infer is to conclude from evidence

indicators.note: the city is full, so it holds inside it the word meaning full

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
all means whole or full, as in all day

explanation.surface: Someone decides New York is packed and finds it hellish.
explanation.walkthrough: INFER, then NY filled with ALL: N(ALL)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernally means in the manner of the inferno, the underworld of the damned.

clue.text: Summons late in the day succeeded securing approval

indicators.note: securing means holding something fast, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: eve is the poetic word for evening
OK signals approval
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone is called in at the end of the day after getting the go-ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Eve is the old poetic word for evening, and S for succeeded comes from family-tree notation.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to call up a memory or feeling, a verb synonym of summons in the third person.

clue.text: I let navy collapse into sleaze

indicators.note: to collapse is to fall to pieces, so these letters break up and re-form

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A commander confesses to letting the fleet sink into corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Venality is openness to bribery, a form of corruption close to sleaze.

clue.text: Extremely keen on money for workers in yard

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outermost letters of the word

parts.note: the first and last letters of keen
ackers is British slang for money, coming on (after) the first piece

explanation.surface: Labourers in a yard are very keen on being paid.
explanation.walkthrough: Ackers is British slang for cash. A knacker's yard is where worn-out horses are slaughtered.
explanation.definitionFit: Knackers are the people who slaughter old horses and render them in a knacker's yard.

clue.text: Truss at last out of mind playing a blinder

indicators.note: playing suggests moving pieces about freely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last out of a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: the final letter of mind

explanation.surface: A sporting figure called Truss performs brilliantly while not in their right mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing a blinder' wants to be one phrase; 'playing' is the shuffle signal and 'a blinder' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust is a magical, dazzling quality, and a blinder is a dazzlingly brilliant performance.

clue.text: Such milk for your health

definitions.meaning: first meaning: milk treated to keep for months unopened
second meaning: what a toast to someone's health wishes them

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests milk is good for you; the second half is a toast-like wish for many years.
explanation.definitionFit: UHT milk is sold as long-life, and a toast to someone's health wishes them many years of living.

clue.text: In hearing, one safely securing capital

indicators.note: in hearing means as perceived by the ear, so a word is judged by its sound

parts.note: one who anchors something securely, said in a non-rhotic British accent

explanation.surface: A listener overhears someone keeping a valuable sum safe.
explanation.walkthrough: With the r's dropped, as in southern British speech, ANCHORER is said just like ANKARA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the seat of government of Turkey, its capital city.

clue.text: One following round for each amateur

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes around the phrase after it

parts.note: next means following
per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: A newcomer takes their turn after a round of drinks has been bought for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a round of drinks; it is the signal that one word goes around another.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur in the sense of a non-expert is unskilled, which is what inexpert means as an adjective.

clue.text: Chanced to get fine gospel record eventually

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
Luke is one of the four Gospels

indicators.note: eventually means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: the last letter of record

explanation.surface: Someone takes a gamble and ends up with a recording of gospel music.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluke something is to achieve it by lucky accident, so fluked means succeeded by chance.

clue.text: Parts of Norfolk and Beds may not understand this speech?

parts.note: the Norfolk Broads are a network of shallow lakes and rivers in eastern England
cots are small beds

explanation.surface: People in Norfolk and Bedfordshire, an English county abbreviated Beds, would struggle to follow this dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' looks like the county abbreviation beside Norfolk, but it means sleeping places.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad Scots is the strong Lowland Scottish dialect, a form of speech hard for southern English ears.

clue.text: Train tickets found when darkness lifts?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rail tickets out and back on the same day
second meaning, read literally: daylight comes back at dawn

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading of a common British ticket type as a phrase about sunrise.
explanation.definitionFit: A day return is a British rail fare for a round trip within one day; at dawn the day literally returns.

clue.text: Systematically searches for coins abroad

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sweeps an area back and forth, as a gundog does
second meaning: 25-cent pieces in the US and Canada

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a coin hunter; it is two unrelated senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to quarter ground is to cover it methodically; as a noun, North American 25-cent pieces.

clue.text: Branch kills American comic

parts.note: to off someone is American slang for killing them
a hoot is a very funny person or thing

explanation.surface: A section of an organisation does away with a US comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is a side shoot growing from a main stem, hence a branch of a family or organisation.

clue.text: Suffragette and me twice going head to head over policy

indicators.note: two copies meeting head to head means the first is turned to face the second

parts.note: two copies of me
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A campaigner for women's votes and the speaker clash repeatedly over policy.
explanation.walkthrough: For the two copies to meet head to head, only the first is turned round; the second reads normally.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmeline Pankhurst led the British campaign for women's votes, the most famous suffragette.

clue.text: Rare animal fur I flaunted

indicators.note: flaunted means waved about showily, so these letters are tossed around

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a fur from an uncommon creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is seldom met with, and so strange or not well known to us.

clue.text: An unkempt person, namely Trump

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely
to ruff is to play a trump card in bridge or whist

explanation.surface: It suggests a scruffy figure identified as the American president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' looks like the politician; it is the card-game verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruff is informal British for an untidy, dishevelled person.

clue.text: Judges predecessor a heavyweight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Bible book that comes just before Judges
second meaning: Anthony ..., the British world heavyweight boxing champion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Judges' is the Old Testament book, not court officials; Anthony Joshua is a British heavyweight boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Joshua immediately precedes Judges, and the boxer is a former world heavyweight champion.

clue.text: Run into bar but eat nothing

indicators.note: into means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a stave is a wooden bar or rod
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone dashes into a pub but has no food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; it is a stick of wood. R goes inside STAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to go without food, so a verb phrase for fasting fits.

clue.text: Fungal disease coats small English apple

indicators.note: coats means covers all round, so one word wraps around the following pair

parts.note: rust is a fungal disease of plants
S is the abbreviation for small
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A blight spreads over a little English apple.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair of abbreviations goes inside the disease just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Russet is a variety of eating apple with rough brownish skin, an example of the fruit.

clue.text: Horror film must occasionally intimidate

parts.note: Hitchcock's 1960 horror film

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the word is used

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of must

explanation.surface: A scary movie has to frighten its audience now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To psych out an opponent is an idiom for unsettling them mentally, so it means to intimidate.

clue.text: God Michelangelo himself captures

indicators.note: captures means holds inside, so the answer is held within the run of words

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Michelangelo painted the deity on the Sistine ceiling, and here he captures him.
explanation.definitionFit: Elohim is a Hebrew name for the deity used in the Old Testament.

clue.text: One sharing a spine with me?

definitions.text: One sharing a spine with me?

parts.words: One sharing a spine with me?
parts.note: surface reading: a creature with the same backbone as the speaker

parts.words: One sharing a spine with me?
parts.note: setter's reading: the spine is a book's, and the speaker is the writer whose name is printed there

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spine' suggests anatomy; it is the back of a book, where the names of everyone who wrote it appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wrote a book jointly with another has their name alongside the other writer's on the cover.

clue.text: For whom Imogen compiles, ensconced here?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: Imogen is the setter, so the solver is the one set for
second meaning: a sofa where one settles comfortably

explanation.walkthrough: Imogen is this puzzle's setter, so the solver is the one set for, a set-ee on the pattern of employee; the question mark covers the coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a sofa, a seat one nestles into; the coinage set-ee names the one a setter sets for.

clue.text: Very boring in hospital department recently

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first pair sits within the department

parts.note: A&E, accident and emergency, is the British hospital casualty department
so means very, as in so good
flat means dull or boring

explanation.surface: Things have been very dull in the hospital ward lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hospital department' is A&E, Britain's accident and emergency unit; the ampersand is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: As of late is an idiom meaning lately, in the recent past.
